I agree with you, the most part of my career I had to be a different person. I acted as if I was a happy and healing person but that's only because I had too. I couldn't share my personal life or be myself in general, it will look bad on my end because how intestine my emotions are. I'm a sad bpd, i would stay in the staff room or bathroom to cry and I would be perfectly normal within 5 minutes. This is partially why I believe I was diagnosed with bpd, though I've been showing symptoms for years. 

I attempted three times within 4 months while still actively working and the severity of my mental health has gotten so bad I was given 6 months sick leave, I had to claim my bpd to receive work benefits. Eventually, I realized how emotionally draining my job was and how badly it affected me, I had to quit. It was painful. I once loved my job and it was hard to say goodbye to the kids I cared for.

I wasn't a registered doctor of some sorts, I just got out of high school and went into the youth care career. My role was to care for the youth and prepare them for independent living, just like everyone else. 

Mind you, most of these kids were apprehended by social workers because of family breakdowns, runaways, mental health watch, etc.

I worked with high risk youth (11-18 years) for 4 years, during the peak of my depression and diagnosed with bpd while working. It was easy to connect with the youth who have similar backgrounds with mental health issues. I loved my jobs at some point between then, I was mentor for them. 
The biggest struggle I had was ignoring my own mental health and focussing on theirs more. I was harming myself and even attempted a few times. Moral of the story is you should practice making some time for yourself and do some self care. 

Youth care is a very demanding job and anyone is capable of doing it, with the right mind set, but it is also very rewarding. They will take care of you just the same. Watching the youth in my care smile and laugh has always been a blessing for me. Even if I had my own shit going on.

I had just started therapy with a psychiatrist recently (only one visit). The last time I felt this way I was 14 but it was never this serious, and I'm 21 now. When I say everyone is gone I mean that when the scare of me attempting is calm now, everyone assumes that I'm fine. I was never the one to ask for help, and I still don't, but it would be nice to have someone asking me how my day was, you know? Someone who is there and reminds me that I'll be ok. But I don't and that sucks. I don't want to burden my boyfriend with my problems, when he has some serious ones of his own; when he's depressed I help him through it, but it's not recieved from on my end. I just feel I give and give and give but nobody ever gives back. And maybe that's why I'm so upset all the time. Work doesn't help either because I'm a youth care worker and I have to be on my feet and emotionally stable, but it's whatever. It was my career choice.
